sourceText: When a `lattice host_run --host codex` run fails, the ledger final only says unavailableReason: "no_turn_completed_usage_event". On 2026-07-11 (story B-3928) the real cause — codex exec emitted {"type":"turn.failed","error":{"message":"...status 400... The gpt-5.6-sol model requires a newer version of Codex..."}} — had to be dug out of a Codex Desktop rollout because host_run retains only turn.completed lines and --ephemeral leaves no codex session file. Improvement: in packages/main/src/core/host-run.ts, extend the codex usage-line retainer/scanner path so that turn.failed (and terminal error) events are also retained (bounded, last-one-wins, same 1MiB cap discipline) and recorded as a more specific honest unavailableReason, e.g. turn_failed(<short digest of error.message>), falling back to no_turn_completed_usage_event when neither event is present. Keep the honest-unavailable semantics (never fabricate usage). Add a pinned fixture for the turn.failed shape to packages/main/src/tasks/host-run-usage-smoke.ts (exact observed line pinned).
normalizedOutcome: A failed codex host_run whose stream carried a turn.failed (or terminal error) event records an unavailable ledger final whose unavailableReason is turn_failed(<short digest of error.message>) instead of the generic no_turn_completed_usage_event; the generic reason remains only when neither event is present; usage is never fabricated and genuine turn.completed usage still records provider-reported; the exact observed B-3928 turn.failed line is pinned as a smoke fixture.
acceptanceClaim: Running the compiled host-run-usage smoke shows: (1) the pinned exact B-3928 turn.failed fixture produces an unavailable final with unavailableReason turn_failed(...) carrying the Codex-upgrade message digest, (2) a stream with neither turn.completed nor failure events still records no_turn_completed_usage_event, and (3) a stream with genuine turn.completed usage still records the provider-reported final unchanged.
